title: Live sockets and presence
summary: Chat and live scores keep a connection open; that changes how you count capacity.

steps.title: Open lines
steps.text: Normal web requests ask and leave. A live feature, like chat, keeps a connection open so the server can push messages the moment they happen. A server can hold tens of thousands of open lines (approx.), but each one uses memory even when quiet.

steps.prompt: Chat messages overwhelm the app servers. Add a websocket gateway to hold the connections.

between.note: The gateway goes between the phones and the servers, so it holds the open connections. Drop it onto that line.

steps.hint: Place a Websocket gateway between the phones and the servers.

steps.title: Who is online
steps.text: Presence ("Sam is online") is a stream of tiny updates. Keep it in memory, expire it fast, and accept that it is a little off. Do not write it to the main database.

steps.q: Why is a live feature costly when users are quiet?
choices: Messages are very large in size
They always need a CDN in front
Every quiet user needs a database
steps.why: Each idle connection still takes a slot.

choices: In memory with a short expiry
steps.why: It changes constantly and is only useful for a moment.

steps.q: A gateway server restarts. What happens to its users?
choices: They are moved to another user
steps.why: Reconnect with random delay so they do not stampede.

takeaway: Count open connections, not just requests, and keep presence light.
